newsitem.title: GERMANY: Six-month building halt could boost peace-Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Six-month building halt could boost peace-Mubarak.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said in a German newspaper interview that a six-month suspension of Jewish settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem could restart the stalled peace process.

Israel's start of construction on the Har Homa settlement last March has brought the already faltering Middle East peace process to a standstill, despite intensive mediation attempts by the United States.

"If the Israelis were prepared to suspend settlement building until negotiations about Jerusalem have started, perhaps for six months, things could look different," Mubarak told the business daily Handelsblatt in an interview released ahead of publication on Tuesday.
Mubarak flew into Germany on Monday for a brief visit, centred on meetings on Tuesday with Chancellor Helmut Kohl and President Roman Herzog.

The Egyptian leader said if Israel observed the Oslo accord, a broad-brush interim agreement that promised security for Israel and self-rule for Palestinians, the Palestinians would be ready to find a compromise formula to settle Jerusalem's status.
"We only need a small sign from Israel," he said, in comments quoted in German.
Mubarak said he would continue his own efforts for peace.
"I have tried everything to give peace a chance. I have sent several messages to (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu, but he insists on Har Homa," Mubarak said.

He added that he had even wanted to send an envoy to see Netanyahu during the latest peace mission by U.S. mediator Dennis Ross to try to find a formula which would be advantageous for Israel. But Netanyahu offered no encouragement, and Mubarak dropped the idea.
Mubarak also said more must be done to bring Syria back into the peace process.
He said late Israeli premier Yitzhak Rabin had told him he was prepared to give up the strategic Israeli-occupied Golan Heights to Syria, but had not wanted to make this public too soon.

While Netanyahu did not appear ready even to contemplate giving up the Golan Heights, Syrian President Hafez al-Assad had made clear he would not re-enter talks with Israel unless this issue was on the table, Mubarak said.
